Kenworthy objects that the Pressburg district, which is predominantly Magyar, has been handed to the new Czechoslovak State so that it may have a riparian frontier on the Danube. He argues that the historic town, with its Magyar population and old Hungarian associations, should not be handed over to alien rule, and he warns that failing to rectify this will cause future warfare. He also says that the drawing of the frontier was made without sufficient regard to the ethnographic facts and was decided by political rather than fair considerations.
